name: Fig Trees
overview: Scripture uses fig trees as powerful symbols of spiritual condition and readiness. From the first use of fig leaves by Adam and Eve to cover their nakedness (Genesis 3:7), to the fig tree's own question of forsaking its sweetness for promotion (Judges 9:11), the fig tree represents both provision and responsibility. Jeremiah contrasts good and bad figs to illustrate moral discernment (Jeremiah 24:2), while Habakkuk highlights the dire consequences when the fig tree fails to blossom, signifying judgment or hardship (Habakkuk 3:17). Christ’s cursing of the barren fig tree (Matthew 21:19) and His parable teaching to observe the fig tree’s budding as a sign of the coming season (Matthew 24:32) further emphasize the importance of fruitfulness and spiritual awareness.
